title: PRD: Runbook-triggered rollback and synthetic verification for graceful degradation
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures product requirements to translate postmortem action items from the 2026-01 regional-serving outage into a PRD chapter focused on two capabilities: (1) runbook-triggered rollback gating for model/route rollouts and autoscale-induced degradation, and (2) a synthetic verification harness that continuously validates service quality after any rollout or autoscale event. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect regressions, shorten MTTD/MTTR, and provide deterministic rollback behavior tied to SLO degradation thresholds.

Background and motivation:
The postmortem identified multiple incidents where customer-facing latency and token error rates increased after rolling a new kernel selection profile and during autoscale cold-start activity. Manual runbook triggers and ad-hoc dashboards delayed safe rollbacks. The engineering postmortem recommended stricter rollout gates, automated rollback triggers, and a synthetic verification layer that exercises representative request shapes immediately after changes. This PRD adds the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan so engineering and design can scope work consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define API surface in Console and API for associating runbooks with rollout plans and model variants.
- Define SLO degradation thresholds that will auto-mark a rollout as unhealthy (latency P95, token-error-rate, generation success %).
- Implement a synthetic verification service that runs post-change traffic against a configurable prompt set and reports quality metrics to Console dashboards and alerting.
- Wire rollback automation to runbook triggers and to the smart-routing fallback layer so traffic can be shifted to previous model variants or lower-cost paths.
- Acceptance tests: load/soak tests, chaos tests (simulated cold start), and synthetic verification passing criteria.

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Full RBAC UI for customers to author runbooks (will be follow-up).
- On-prem packaged agent for environments without control plane connectivity (limited shim is acceptable).

Stakeholders:
- Product: Asha Raman (owner), Priya Singh (reliability PM)
acceptance_criteria: Console: ability to attach a runbook ID and a rollback policy to any rollout plan; UI shows current runbook status after rollout
SLOs: declarative thresholds configured per-route (examples: P95 latency > 300ms, token-error-rate > 0.5%) that mark rollout as unhealthy

Automation: when synthetic verification fails or SLO thresholds breach within the defined evaluation window, the system must automatically trigger rollback action within 2 minutes or escalate via the runbook
Synthetic harness: supports configurable prompt sets (min 20 prompts), configurable evaluation window (1–30 minutes), and returns pass/fail with metric breakdowns to the Console
Observability: dashboards and traces show synthetic test results, rollout status, and precise rollback reason with links to the runbook and offending change (PR/commit/hash)

Testing: end-to-end CI job that performs a canary rollout in a staging env and runs synthetic verification; job must exercise cold-starts and validate no >10% degradation vs baseline in generation quality metrics
Compatibility: feature must work for Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (control-plane-assisted) deployments
Audit trail: all automated rollback actions, synthetic test results, and manual runbook steps must be logged with timestamps and operator identity
decisions: Use a lightweight synthetic runner in the control plane that can be optionally proxied for Private customers
Rollback granularity: per-route + per-model-variant (not per-request), to keep state manageable
Evaluation window default will be 5 minutes with a configurable 1–30 minute range
Synthetic prompt sets must include at least one long-sequence prompt to exercise KV cache behavior
risks: Synthetic tests may produce false positives due to upstream model nondeterminism; need baselining and conservative thresholds
Automated rollbacks could oscillate if the synthetic harness is noisy; mitigation: require 2 consecutive failing windows unless operator overrides
Private deployments with limited telemetry may need a degraded mode that relies on local verification agents
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement API + synthetic harness in staging; run 2 weeks of synthetic baseline collection; validate against 3 historical incidents
Phase 2 (beta): expose runbook attachment and automated rollback for internal teams and 2 select customers; collect feedback and tune thresholds
Phase 3 (GA): enable opt-in default for all Hosted accounts, provide docs and runbook templates; Dedicated and Private enabled with customer consent
Phase 4 (post-GA): add RBAC UI for custom runbook authoring and a local verification shim for fully air-gapped environments
implementation_notes: ENG-7884 to implement synthetic runner service and mock prompt execution
ENG-8250 to add rollback orchestration hooks in smart-routing
Need a short RFC for the rollback policy DSL to avoid ambiguity between canary-size and rollback aggressiveness
Telemetry schema: add fields for synthetic_test_id, baseline_hash, failure_reason
metrics_and_success: Reduction of manual rollback time: target 50% decrease in mean time to rollback for incidents matching the postmortem class
Decrease in customer-visible incident duration by 30% for rollout-related degradations
Synthetic harness false positive rate < 5% after two weeks of baseline tuning
Number of automated rollbacks executed per month (target: 0–3 after tuning) monitored for oscillation
